title: Object-Oriented Thinking
author: Vaysfeld
tldr: Comprehensive guide to object-oriented programming paradigm covering fundamental concepts (classes, inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, abstraction), practical design patterns, and best practices for building maintainable and scalable systems. The book emphasizes the importance of proper abstraction, separation of concerns, and thinking in terms of objects rather than procedures.

core_concepts.definition: Paradigm based on concept of objects that contain data (attributes) and code (methods)
Blueprint or template for creating objects, defining structure and behavior
Mechanism allowing classes to inherit properties and methods from parent classes
Ability of objects to take multiple forms or for methods to behave differently based on context
Bundling of data and methods together while hiding implementation details
Process of hiding complexity by showing only necessary features
Reusable solutions to common problems in object-oriented design
Principle of using object composition instead of inheritance for greater flexibility

key_takeaways: Think in terms of objects and their responsibilities, not procedures
Design classes with single responsibility and cohesive behavior
Use inheritance to model 'is-a' relationships carefully
Prefer composition over inheritance for flexibility
Apply design patterns to solve recurring design problems
Encapsulation protects internal state and ensures consistency
Proper abstraction reduces complexity and improves maintainability
Polymorphism enables flexible and extensible designs

applications.applicability: High - Direct application to code design and implementation
High - System design and component relationships
High - Code review standards and mentoring

prerequisites: Understanding of fundamental programming concepts (variables, functions, control flow)
Familiarity with at least one programming language
